result.title: SPADE-KD: Peer-to-Peer Collaborative Learning under Heterogeneous Settings
result.summary: Peer-to-peer collaborative learning is an emerging distributed deep learning paradigm that eliminates the need for a central aggregator and disseminator, avoiding the single-point-of-failure and bottleneck issues they can bring. Many such approaches use parameter averaging, requiring clients to have homogeneous model architectures, whereas others use knowledge distillation as an alternative while leaning on shared public data or centralized control infrastructure. Many of these approaches also make a one-size-fits-all assumption, i.e., jointly training a single, globally optimal solution for all clients, when in reality, clients' underlying data distributions might differ such that a globally optimal solution may not be locally optimal for all clients. To enable collaborative learning in environments with both model architecture and data distribution heterogeneity, we present SPADE-KD -- a fully decentralized model distillation framework that optimizes collaboration towards personalized rather than global performance. SPADE-KD leverages two mechanisms -- adaptive distillation and utility-driven peer selection. Adaptive distillation modulates the strength of each incoming model transfer by the performance advantage of the incoming model compared to the native model measured by their task losses, such that a client will distill more aggressively from incoming models that outperform it on its own local data. Utility-driven peer selection uses the loss-informed utility derived from adaptive distillation to rank prospective partners, focusing on exchanges that measurably improve the local model while suppressing low-utility transfers. Using federated classification tasks, we demonstrate that SPADE-KD consistent outperforms naive decentralized distillation with lower loss and faster convergence and that its individual components are more effective together than independently.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SPADE-KD，一个完全去中心化的知识蒸馏框架，通过自适应蒸馏强度与基于效用的对等方选择，在模型结构与数据分布异构下实现个性化联邦协同学习。
AI.relevance_reason: 讨论的是分布式客户端间的模型迁移与个性化权重，不涉及视觉或多模态推理状态、证据获取与停止决策；其「效用驱动的迁移筛选」虽与贡献分配有表面相似，但作用对象是外部模型而非内部 latent 推理过程，缺乏可核查的具体借鉴线索。
